stories.title: Citrix NetScaler: check exposure and investigate compromise

bullets.text: The Canadian Cyber Centre warns of critical vulnerabilities affecting NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway.
bullets.quote: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of critical vulnerabilities affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances.

bullets.text: A remote attacker could execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable appliance without authenticating.
bullets.quote: The vulnerability may allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable NetScaler appliance.

bullets.text: Preserve forensic evidence before rebooting, patching, or rebuilding affected appliances, where feasible.
bullets.quote: Preserve forensic evidence before shutting down, rebooting, patching, rebuilding, or otherwise modifying affected appliances, where feasible.

bullets.text: CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772. That signal applies to those CVEs, not every related issue.
bullets.quote: CISA KEV matched CVEs: CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772

details.text: The Canadian Cyber Centre warns of critical vulnerabilities affecting NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway.
details.quote: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of critical vulnerabilities affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances.

stories.title: Lantronix: check device versions and apply the matching fix

bullets.text: CISA warns that successful exploitation could bypass authentication and run code with root-level privileges.
bullets.quote: Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to bypass authentication and execute code with root-level privileges.

bullets.text: One affected product is EDS5000 through 2.1.0.0R3. Check the complete product table before acting.
bullets.quote: Lantronix EDS5000 series: <=2.1.0.0R3

bullets.text: For EDS5000, upgrade to 2.2.0.0R1 or later. This fix is specific to that family.
bullets.quote: EDS5000 series: Upgrade to version 2.2.0.0R1 or later.

bullets.text: CISA KEV lists CVE-2025-67038. Do not interpret that as exploitation of every vulnerability in this advisory.
bullets.quote: CISA KEV matched CVEs: CVE-2025-67038

details.text: CISA describes vulnerabilities that could permit authentication bypass and code execution with root-level privileges if successfully exploited. Treat this as the stated technical impact, not proof that a particular device was compromised.
details.quote: Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to bypass authentication and execute code with root-level privileges.

details.text: The supplied affected-product list includes EDS5000 releases through 2.1.0.0R3. This boundary is specific to EDS5000; do not apply it to other Lantronix families. The source contains the complete product and version list.
details.quote: Lantronix EDS5000 series: <=2.1.0.0R3

details.text: For the EDS5000 series, the stated fix is version 2.2.0.0R1 or later. Match the actual device family and release to the source guidance rather than treating that version as a universal Lantronix fix.
details.quote: EDS5000 series: Upgrade to version 2.2.0.0R1 or later.

stories.title: Cisco NGOAM: remote code execution risk on affected Nexus switches

bullets.text: Cisco describes possible unauthenticated code execution or denial of service.
bullets.quote: Multiple vulnerabilities in the Operation, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) feature of Cisco NX-OS Software, known as Next Generation OAM (NGOAM), could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges or cause a denial of service (DoS) condition on an affected device.

bullets.text: Nexus 3000/9000 standalone NX-OS exposure depends on NGOAM and vulnerability-specific conditions.
bullets.quote: These vulnerabilities affect Cisco Nexus 3000 Series Switches and Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches in standalone NX-OS mode if NGOAM is enabled and specific features are configured, as detailed in the following list:

bullets.text: If NGOAM is not required, Cisco says disabling it removes the attack vector.
bullets.quote: If the NGOAM feature is not required, disabling it removes the attack vector and is a mitigation for all three vulnerabilities.

bullets.text: Cisco PSIRT reports no known public announcements or malicious use.
bullets.quote: The Cisco Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is not aware of any public announcements or malicious use of the vulnerabilities that are described in this advisory.

stories.title: SonicWall SMA1000: reported exploitation requires careful attribution

bullets.text: BleepingComputer reports exploitation of CVE-2026-102255 in SMA1000 appliances.
bullets.quote: Attackers are exploiting a maximum-severity vulnerability in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances (CVE-2026-102255) that was patched on Tuesday, three days ago.

bullets.text: The named models are SMA1000 6210, 7210, and 8200v; the excerpt excludes SMA100 and firewall SSL-VPN.
bullets.quote: Tracked as CVE-2026-102255 , the flaw affects the Appliance WorkPlace interface on SMA1000 6210, 7210, and 8200v models, but does not affect the SMA 100 Series product line or SSL-VPN running on SonicWall firewalls.

bullets.text: A researcher reports honeypot attempts consistent with the flaw; vendor confirmation differs.
bullets.quote: While SonicWall has not yet flagged this vulnerability as actively exploited in its Tuesday advisory, Previdian founder and security researcher Ryan Dewhurst told BleepingComputer on Friday that the company's honeypot network has detected exploitation attempts consistent with the CVE-2026-102255 flaw.

details.text: BleepingComputer reports attacks against a maximum-severity SMA1000 vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-102255. Treat the exploitation statement as publisher-attributed reporting; the detailed source distinguishes the vendor’s advisory from a researcher’s observations.
details.quote: Attackers are exploiting a maximum-severity vulnerability in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances (CVE-2026-102255) that was patched on Tuesday, three days ago.

details.text: The article identifies the Appliance WorkPlace interface on SMA1000 6210, 7210, and 8200v. It explicitly says the issue does not affect the SMA100 Series or SSL-VPN on SonicWall firewalls. Exact affected software releases are not supplied here.
details.quote: Tracked as CVE-2026-102255 , the flaw affects the Appliance WorkPlace interface on SMA1000 6210, 7210, and 8200v models, but does not affect the SMA 100 Series product line or SSL-VPN running on SonicWall firewalls.

details.text: The quoted source says SonicWall had not flagged active exploitation in the Tuesday advisory, while researcher Ryan Dewhurst reported honeypot activity consistent with this CVE to BleepingComputer. Preserve both statements rather than presenting them as a single vendor-confirmed conclusion.
details.quote: While SonicWall has not yet flagged this vulnerability as actively exploited in its Tuesday advisory, Previdian founder and security researcher Ryan Dewhurst told BleepingComputer on Friday that the company's honeypot network has detected exploitation attempts consistent with the CVE-2026-102255 flaw.
